ticket.confidence_notes: CONTROLLED STAKE (50% Allocation — 2,000 FCFA). Compound probability is 54.4%, placing the ticket squarely in the medium confidence bracket (50.0% - 59.9%). The ticket deploys Archetype 1 (The Mismatch Dominance Pair) under Model 5.1 Track A (Continental Club Competitions), leveraging Section 3.7 (Dominant Home Winner Promotion Protocol). By pairing UEFA Champions League #1 ranked Paris Saint-Germain (100% win rate, +15 GD, averaging 5.0 GF/G @ 1.50 vs AS Roma, Dominance Ratio 3.80) with Inter Milan Home Win (@ 1.39 vs VfB Stuttgart, 87.5% San Siro home win record, Dominance Ratio 4.46), the ticket hits 2.09 combined odds with only 2 legs, completely eliminating accumulator drag while bypassing hazardous away rotation traps (Bayern Munich's injury crisis with Harry Kane and Michael Olise sidelined, and Liverpool's road volatility at Jan Breydel Stadium). Cumulative value edge +6.4pp and ticket expected value +13.4%.
ticket.notes: Two-leg Champions League accumulator ticket constructed under Model 5.1 (roys_tournament_international_engine) and selection_process_tournament.md (Section 3.1 Archetype 1: Mismatch Dominance Pair & Section 3.7 Dominant Home Winner Promotion Protocol). Features Paris Saint-Germain vs AS Roma Home Win 1X2 (@ 1.50, 73.0% Calibrated Model Prob, +6.3pp Edge, EV +0.095) paired with Inter Milan vs VfB Stuttgart Home Win 1X2 (@ 1.39, 74.5% Calibrated Model Prob, +2.6pp Edge, EV +0.036). Combined odds: 2.09 vs compound probability 54.4% (break-even 48.0%, cumulative value edge +6.4pp, ticket EV +0.134).

selections.comment: Clinical 2-0 home win at San Siro. Inter controlled the tie without Calhanoglu and extended their fortress record to 8W-0D-1L at home.
selections.notes: UEFA Champions League Matchday 5 clash at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza (San Siro). Inter Milan has rebounded powerfully from an early European stumble with back-to-back clean-sheet victories (including a 3-0 away win over Feyenoord) and has won 6 of their last 8 matches overall. At the San Siro, Inter is an imposing fortress this season, posting 7 wins in 8 home fixtures (W7, D0, L1, 87.5% win rate, zero draws). VfB Stuttgart enters on a continental downturn, taking 0 points from their last 2 UCL matches and failing to score in a 2-0 defeat away at Galatasaray. Furthermore, Stuttgart historically struggles on Italian soil, managing just 1 win in their last 9 trips to Italy (D2, L6). Net Elo gap is +260 points (Inter 1,950 venue-adjusted vs Stuttgart 1,690) and Dominance Ratio is 4.46 (6.20 / 1.39). Break-even 71.9% vs Calibrated Win Probability 74.5% delivers a +2.6pp value edge and +3.6% EV.

warnings.description: VfB Stuttgart has a chronic historical deficit when traveling to Italian grounds in European competition.
warnings.evidence: Stuttgart has won only 1 of their last 9 away matches in Italy (D2, L6) and lost 2-0 away at Galatasaray on Matchday 4.
warnings.review_notes: Stuttgart's poor European road form in Italy continued as they were held scoreless in a 2-0 defeat at Inter Milan, registering their second straight 2-0 away UCL loss.

warnings.review_notes: Hakan Çalhanoğlu's absence did not disrupt Inter Milan's control or finishing, as the Nerazzurri comfortably won 2-0 with a clean sheet at the San Siro.

selections.comment: SHOOTOUT DRAW TRAP: Match finished 2-2 (4 goals). Model prioritized 73.0% Home Win 1X2 over 78.5% Over 2.5 @ 1.35 despite Roma averaging 2.50 GF/G in the UCL.
selections.notes: UEFA Champions League Matchday 5 marquee clash at Parc des Princes. Paris Saint-Germain sits joint-top of the 36-team single table with a perfect 12 points from 4 matches (4-0-0), scoring an astounding 20 goals (5.0 GF/G) with a +15 goal difference. Luis Enrique's squad possesses the competition's highest Sofascore team rating (8.21), having dismantled Villarreal 6-0 away in their previous European outing. AS Roma sits in 20th place with 4 points (1-1-2), leaking 8 goals across 4 games (conceding 3 to Real Madrid and 3 to Manchester United). Net Elo gap is +280 points (PSG 2,000 venue-adjusted vs Roma 1,720), and Dominance Ratio is 3.80 (5.70 / 1.50), comfortably exceeding the 3.0 threshold. Model projects a 73.0% home win probability against break-even 66.7%, yielding an outstanding +6.3pp value edge and +9.5% EV.

warnings.description: PSG has maintained a 100% win record in the 2026/27 Champions League with overwhelming offensive firepower.
warnings.evidence: 4 wins in 4 matches, 20 goals scored (5.0 GF/G), and an average player rating of 8.21 across the tournament.
warnings.review_notes: PSG scored twice at Parc des Princes but conceded 2 goals to draw 2-2 with AS Roma, ending their 100% Champions League winning streak and failing to deliver Home Win dominance.

warnings.description: AS Roma has shown chronic defensive vulnerabilities against elite continental offenses.

warnings.review_notes: AS Roma conceded 2 goals in Paris in line with their 2.0 GA/G UCL average, but counter-punched with 2 goals of their own (2-2) to avoid defeat.

alternatives.comment: Strictly disqualified under Rule 12 (LINEUP_SPINE_COMPROMISED) and Rule 17. Lille's defensive low block makes Bayern Away Win @ 1.60 a high-variance trap.
alternatives.notes: Classic tournament favorite trap. Without Kane's focal point (>40% of Bayern goal contributions) and Olise's chance creation, Bayern's goal expectancy drops dramatically, shifting value toward Lille or Draw (+1 AH). Bayern 1X2 @ 1.60 carries severe -8.5pp negative EV.

warnings.description: Bayern Munich's primary goalscorer Harry Kane is ruled out for several months with a severe syndesmosis ankle tear.
warnings.evidence: Kane and Michael Olise confirmed sidelined; Kompany forced to deploy improvised, depleted frontline.
warnings.review_notes: Without Harry Kane and Michael Olise, Bayern Munich's depleted attack managed just 1 goal and suffered a 2-1 upset loss at Lille, completely validating the CRITICAL spine-compromise disqualification.

warnings.review_notes: Shorthanded Bayern Munich lost 2-1 in northern France, fully confirming that backing them as a 1.60 away favorite (-8.5pp EV) was a severe trap.

alternatives.comment: Shadow alternative to PSG straight win. PSG averages 5.0 goals per game in Europe and Roma has leaked 8 goals in 4 matches, delivering a 78.5% Over 2.5 probability (+4.4pp edge); however, PSG Home Win 1X2 @ 1.50 was prioritized on the main ticket, and dual-exposure on the same match is prohibited.
alternatives.notes: Pristine goal expectancy selection satisfying Model 5.1 Rule 13 (Dual-Scoring Floor: PSG GF* 3.50 >= 1.10, Roma GF* 2.00 >= 1.10, DCI 0.57 >= 0.45). Relegated to shadow tracking exclusively to avoid single-match correlation drag.

warnings.description: PSG 1X2 already occupies primary ticket capital; stacking Over 2.5 on the same fixture introduces unnecessary correlation risk.
warnings.evidence: Model 5.1 limits active capital to exactly one market per match fixture.
warnings.review_notes: Portfolio governance rule (not an on-pitch risk). Notably, Over 2.5 @ 1.35 won easily in the 2-2 draw while PSG 1X2 lost, showing Over 2.5 (78.5% prob) should have been prioritized over 1X2 (73.0% prob).

alternatives.comment: Relegated to shadow tracking because the primary ticket achieved its 2.09 target in 2 legs via PSG and Inter home victories. Sporting CP is in supreme form (5-game winning run under Paulo Fonseca, Luis Suarez 4 goals in 4 UCL matches), while United misses the suspended Matheus Cunha.
alternatives.notes: Strong resilience selection under Archetype 2. Sporting boasts a much tighter European defensive record (4 goals conceded vs United's 8 conceded). Over 1.5 @ 1.16 was disqualified under Rule 8.

warnings.review_notes: Sporting CP avoided defeat in a 2-2 draw to cash Double Chance 1X @ 1.55, though Manchester United still managed to score twice in Lisbon despite Matheus Cunha's suspension.

alternatives.notes: Both teams sit level in 8th and 9th place in the UCL standings. Club Brugge's fortress form at Jan Breydel Stadium creates acute draw friction, making Liverpool an unviable 1X2 play.
